moat_against: ROIC proxy fell 23.1% (2020) → 6.6% (2025); gross margin band 33.3–38.8% shows no through-cycle pricing power
C&I/data-center faces Cummins and Caterpillar with deeper diesel franchises and no Generac share dominance
Residential demand is hostage to exogenous outage/weather activity
Clean-energy (PWRcell) capital consumption without a second established moat
moat_for: >70% share of the US home standby generator category — the default brand for a dealer-installed, infrequent purchase
Extensive dealer/installer and retail distribution network that is expensive to replicate
Installed base feeds parts, service and monitoring attach
Scale in large-megawatt gensets converting into hyperscale data-center agreements ($1.6B backlog at Q2 2026)
moat_justification: Dominant >70% US home standby share, brand and dealer network are genuine, but ROIC proxy fell from 23.1% (2020) to 6.6% (2025), gross margin oscillates 33–39% with no through-cycle pricing power, and the C&I/data-center growth leg is contested by Cummins/Caterpillar where Generac holds no share dominance.
name: Generac Holdings Inc.
one_liner: Real home-standby franchise (70%+ share, moat 5/10) but fading returns — ROIC 23.1%→6.6% in five years — and at $192.68 (~35x TTM OE) even the super-bull case earns 11.8%; Tier D, clears 15% only below $71.13.
sector: Industrials / Capital Goods — backup power generation
